behavioral_notes.observation: XML-IDs ('module.name') are resolved to (res_model, res_id) by a SQL lookup on ir_model_data; this is how ref='module.xml_id' in data files, views and Python resolves to a live database row. Every record loaded from XML/CSV gets an ir.model.data row, which also anchors modular upgrade and clean uninstall. The mapping is pure data, invisible to field metadata. Live: 6828 ir.model.data rows.

res.users uses delegation inheritance (_inherits), not classical _inherit: a user record transparently exposes its res.partner fields (name, email, lang, address, avatar) through partner_id. A user IS-A partner at the data layer; deleting/merging must account for the shared partner. SELF_READABLE_FIELDS / SELF_WRITEABLE_FIELDS gate what a user may read/write on their own record. Not derivable from field metadata alone.

Odoo's ORM persists its own schema: one ir.model row per model and one ir.model.fields row per field. The registry describes itself in its own tables, which is what makes models/fields introspectable, extensible at runtime (Studio custom fields), and what ir.model.access / ir.rule attach security to via model_id. Live: 129 ir.model + 1645 ir.model.fields rows on a fresh DB.

res.company is self-referential (parent_id/child_ids) with computed parent_path, parent_ids and root_id; multi-company scoping (company_ids on res.users, company_id on most documents) is enforced via _check_company_domain and record rules defined here. The branch/root company tree underpins multi-company record isolation across the whole ERP. Not visible in metadata.

On a freshly initialized DB base alone populates 43 of 67 probed models: ir.model.data=6828, res.country.state=2131, ir.model.fields=1645, ir.module.module.dependency=1400, ir.model.fields.selection=854, ir.module.module=670, ir.model.constraint=376, res.country=251, ir.ui.view=229, ir.model.access=152, ir.model=129; and exactly 1 res.company (My Company), 1 res.currency (USD), 1 res.lang (en_US), 1 res.users (Administrator). This is the kernel/reference-data substrate every other module builds on.

base ships effectively zero frontend: 0 JS files, 0 XML/OWL templates, 0 registry adds, 0 patches; only a single web.assets_tests bundle entry. All backend UI (web client, OWL) lives in the separate 'web' module — base is a pure server/ORM/data kernel with no client-side code.

classification.rationale: base is the firm's IT infrastructure expressed in software: it provides the ORM/data model, the security and access-control engine, user/company/identity primitives, module lifecycle, scheduling, and storage. By Stabell & Fjeldstad it is a pure 'support' value model (firm infrastructure / technology development), never a primary value-creating activity. auto_install=true and depends=[] confirm it is the kernel every other subsystem rests on. APQC 8.0 'Manage IT' fits best because base literally implements the application platform, data management, and security administration; an argument exists for 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities' since base also DEFINES the Organization domain (res.users/res.groups) and Information-Concept primitives (res.partner/res.company/res.currency), but 8.0 is the dominant character of an ORM+security+module-management kernel, so 8.0 is chosen with 13.0 noted as secondary.

standard_capabilities: XML-ID registry for modular data, upgrade and uninstall (ir.model.data)
model-level ACLs + domain-based record rules (ir.model.access, ir.rule)
users, groups, privileges, API keys, multi-company (res.users, res.groups, res.company)
world reference data: currencies, countries+states, languages
scheduled jobs (ir.cron), attachments/filestore (ir.attachment), sequences, QWeb engine
typical_fits: standard partner/company/user model reused unchanged by every module
group-based security with multi-company record-rule isolation out of the box
common_gaps: custom security groups / record rules for bespoke access policies
additional reference data or company-specific currency rate feeds
extending res.partner / res.users via _inherit for industry-specific fields
external IdP / SSO and advanced password policy (typically add-on modules)
